newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish telecoms firms see big interconnect cuts.
newsitem.headline: Danish telecoms firms see big interconnect cuts.

text.p: Telecoms operators competing with Tele Danmark said on Monday that they foresaw major cuts in network interconnection access rates when new deregulation legislation came into force in the spring.

"I expect the interconnection rates that competitors will have to pay Tele Danmark for access to its telephone network to fall to around 0.06 to 0.08 crowns per minute compared to today's 0.18 crowns," Claus Jacobsen, Swedish operator Telia's managing director in Denmark, told Reuters.
Netcom Systems Danmark, another Swedish-based operator active in Denmark, agreed that rates would fall.

"Only with reasonably priced access to Tele Danmark's network can customers benefit fully from increased competition in the industry. Interconnect rates are far too high at the moment," Netcom Systems managing director Ebbe Joergensen said.

The Danish government is currently working on a bill to liberalise interconnect deals as part of the current deregulation of the country's telecoms industry and the legislation is expected to be in place by the end of March.
In February Tele Danmark protested by letter against the government's proposed telecommunications legislation.
It claimed the draft bill would pave the way for much lower rates for competitor access to its network than European Union stipulations and threatened to hit profits hard.
Denmark's telecommunications union said last week that the legislation could mean a direct drop in profits for Tele Danmark of around one billion crowns annually.
The Danish telecommunications sector was deregulated on July 1, 1996, and a second phase of enabling legislation is due to go through parliament soon.
